subject: humanities
passage: Before the 1840s, painters usually stored oil paint in pig bladders, which were difficult to seal and to carry. The collapsible metal tube, patented in 1841, kept paint fresh and portable, and art historian Clara Duvall argues that it made Impressionism possible: freed from the studio, painters such as Claude Monet could set up their easels outdoors and record shifting light directly in front of their subjects.
passage_b: Portable paint certainly encouraged painting outdoors, and the Impressionists made much of their work in the open air. Yet the image of the Impressionist completing every canvas on the spot is misleading. Monet, for instance, began his paintings of Rouen Cathedral in front of the building but reworked many of them for months in his studio. The tube changed where a painting could begin; it did not end the role of the studio.
stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: Most Impressionist paintings were completed in the studio rather than outdoors.
choices.B: Before 1841, painters were unable to work outdoors at all.
choices.C: The metal paint tube made it easier for painters to work outdoors.
choices.D: Monet's paintings of Rouen Cathedral show that the tube freed painters from the studio.

explanation.why: Text 1 says the tube "kept paint fresh and portable" so painters could work outdoors. Text 2 agrees that "Portable paint certainly encouraged painting outdoors." The authors differ on how far the studio lost its role, but both accept that the tube made outdoor painting easier.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says only that the idea of finishing every canvas outdoors is misleading; it does not say most were finished in the studio, and Text 1 would disagree.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 1 says paint in bladders was hard to carry, not that outdoor work was impossible, and Text 2 does not address the point.
explanation.C: Correct. Both texts agree that portable tube paint encouraged painters to work in the open air.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 uses the Rouen Cathedral paintings to show the studio's continuing role, the opposite of this claim.
